title: Nvidia in talks to invest further in Reflection AI or buy it, FT reports
source_used: The Economic Times (carrying the Reuters wire text on the Financial Times report); Startup Fortune for background. The Reuters page itself returned HTTP 401.
key_facts: The Financial Times reported on Saturday 10 Oct 2026, citing people with direct knowledge, that Nvidia is in talks to deepen its investment in the start-up Reflection AI or acquire it.

Talks are at an early stage; one form the deal could take is an acqui-hire, where Nvidia hires staff and licenses technology instead of buying the company, potentially avoiding a lengthy regulatory review.
An agreement could be reached in the coming weeks, but the discussions could still fall apart.
Nvidia has already invested $800 million in Reflection, according to the FT.
Reflection was founded in 2024 by former DeepMind researchers Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou.
Laskin told CNBC in April that Reflection was raising fresh capital at a pre-money valuation of $25 billion.
Reflection launched its first open-weight model, Beam, on Monday 5 Oct 2026 to compete in coding and agent tasks with lower-cost Chinese models such as DeepSeek and Kimi.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report; Nvidia and Reflection had not responded to requests for comment.
quote_evidence: Nvidia is in talks to deepen its investment in open-source startup Reflection AI or acquire it, the Financial Times reported on Saturday, citing people with direct knowledge of the matter.
An agreement could be reached in the coming weeks, according to the report, which cited multiple people familiar with the matter, while adding that the discussions could still fall apart.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
why_it_matters_hint: Nvidia, the main maker of AI chips, may take full ownership of a leading US developer of open-weight models it already funds; the talks are early and unconfirmed.
notes: Reuters link is blocked here (HTTP 401); text read on The Economic Times, which carries the Reuters wire text, and cross-checked with Startup Fortune, which says Bloomberg also reported Nvidia weighing more investment or a computing deal (not read directly). Original reporter is the Financial Times. Startup Fortune says the $25 billion was Reflection's last round valuation; Reuters says Laskin said in April it was raising at a $25 billion pre-money valuation, so the entry does not state it as a closed round. Our 6 Oct 2026 edition carried Reflection's Beam launch.
